{{short description|British physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Michael Anthony Flemming''' (born 1948) is a British physicist.  He was educated at King George V GS, Southport, from where he gained a place to read Physics at [[New College, Oxford]], specializing in solid-state physics and electronics.  He continued his doctoral studies in the Electronics Department at [[Southampton University]], where he used the [[micro-electronics]] facility to fabricate high-frequency transistors and developed a test facility based on miniaturised [[microstrip]] probes - a technique which has subsequently formed a basis for commercial [[Wafer (electronics)|wafer probing]] systems.

Following conferment of his PhD,<ref>{{Cite book|title = Measurement Techniques for the Modelling of U.H.F. Integrated-Circuit Components|last = Flemming|first = M A|publisher = University of Southampton|year = 1975}}</ref> he joined the Plessey Radar Research Centre, where he carried out pioneering work on [[Nonlinear junction detector|Harmonic Radar]].<ref>{{Cite book|title = Harmonic Radar Detection Systems|last = Flemming|first = M A|date = October 1977|location = Proceedings of the IEE International Conference RADAR-77|pages = 1223–1231|display-authors=etal}}</ref>  This has found applications in several fields where [[transponder]]s are needed to allow tracking of small objects; one example is the monitoring of bee populations.<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Tracking bees with harmonic radar|last = Riley|first = J R|date = 4 January 1996|journal = Nature |volume=379 |issue = 6560|pages=29–30|doi = 10.1038/379029b0|display-authors=etal|bibcode = 1996Natur.379...29R| s2cid=4260064 }}</ref>

He then worked at the [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment|UKAEA Harwell]] research laboratory, where he led the Radio Frequency and [[Microwave]] Section. He was awarded the [[Duddell Medal and Prize]] by the [[Institute of Physics]] in 1993 for his work on the application of microwave [[ellipsometry]] to the detection of thin surface films of oil on water.<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Microwave Remote Sensing Techniques for measuring Thin Surface Films|last = Flemming|first = M. A.|date = September 1987|journal = Proceedings of the 17th European Microwave Conf., Rome}}</ref>
